extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and editors interested in Korean War reporting
extracted.subtask_description: An Associated Press wartime news dispatch reporting battlefield developments, military communiqués, and statements from commanders during the early Korean War (late June–early July). Intended to inform the public about troop movements, combat actions, and official positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observance of rules of war in treatment of prisoners
rubrics_metrics.description: "PERSONNEL OF THE ARMED FOR F NORTH KOREA AND OTHER PERSONS OF NORTH KOREA WHO ARE TAKEN INTO CUSTODY OR FALL INTO THE HANDS OF ARMED FORCES NOW UNDER MY OPERATIONAL CONTROL IN CONNECTION WITH HOSTILITIES IN KOREA WILL BE TREATED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE HUMANITARIAN PRINCIPLES APPLIED BY AND RECOGNIZED BY CIVILIZED NATIONS INVOLVED IN ARMED CONFLICT." (Text of General MacArthur's statement)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MacArthur's statement: expects similar treatment for American and allied personnel; operating pursuant to U.N. resolutions and as commander will "HOLD RESPONSIBLE ANY INDIVIDUAL ... WHO DEVIATES FROM THESE PRINCIPLES OR WHO CAUSES ... OR ORDERS ANY DEVIATION FROM SUCH PRINCIPLES." This functions as an explicit standard of humane treatment and accountability for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution against reporting unconfirmed foreign participation
rubrics_metrics.description: "WE HAVE YET TO GET REALLY POSITIVE CONFIRMATION OF ANY RUSSIAN PARTICIPATION. UNTIL WE CAPTURE SOME AND PROVE THEY ARE RUSSIANS WE HAVE BEEN TOLD TO STOP REPORTING THAT ANY ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military/press guidance urging reporters and spokesmen not to assert foreign (e.g., Russian) participation without positive proof (capture and confirmation). The surrounding text shows reliance on confirmed captures before attributing belligerent nationality — an explicit standard for responsible reporting of foreign involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to include in military communiqués and war reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples repeatedly shown in communiqués: time and location stamps, descriptions of enemy movements and flanking/enveloping maneuvers, status of key positions (e.g., Suwon, Inchon, Seoul), numbers of sorties flown (e.g., "TO DATE A TOTAL OF 953 SORTIES HAVE BEEN MADE BY THE AIR FORCES"), enemy losses (e.g., "NORTH KOREAN LOSSES CONSISTED OF THREE TRUCKS, ONE BUS AND TWO LOCOMOTIVES"), and casualty/status reports (missing, captured).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dispatch demonstrates a de facto template for military communiqués and frontline reporting: include precise timestamps, operational descriptions (movements, flanking, objectives), quantifiable operational metrics (sorties, vehicles/locomotives destroyed), reported enemy losses, and current status of engagements/positions. Use of concrete figures and named locations provides clarity; unconfirmed claims are flagged or withheld.
